messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>

Cc: Marcus Lee <mlee@clearpay.io>
Date: Fri, 31 Jul 2027 16:12:00 -0700
Subject: Clearpay post-demo: first-frame (TTFT) & streaming ops recap

Thanks again for jumping on the call today — appreciated the thorough walkthrough of the fraud-check flow. Quick recap and proposed next steps on the performance side so we all have alignment before the pilot: 

Summary of what we heard from you
- Peak check volume: ~1.2k checks/sec during peak batch windows; typical sustained load ~300-500 req/sec.
- Typical request payload: 1.8–2.2 KB JSON, with occasional long customer notes (~8–10 KB).
- Strong preference for sub-200ms perceived latency for your UX (want first visible token to appear quickly).

Redwood SLO candidates (initial proposal)
- First-frame (time-to-first-token) median < 120 ms, p95 < 360 ms for standard payloads (<=3 KB).
- For large payloads (>5 KB) median < 200 ms, p95 < 600 ms.
- Target concurrency for pilot: 1,000 concurrent streams (we'll size burst capacity to ~1.5x).
- Token throughput: aim to sustain ~30k tokens/sec across the pool for this workload (estimates based on your prompt mix).

Streaming mode recommendation
- Prefer SSE for browser clients (simpler reconnects) but WebSocket if you need binary framing / lower overhead for many small messages. We recommend starting pilot on SSE and keep WS as fallback.
- Chunk cadence suggestion: 40–80 ms emit window for small interactive responses, or 128–256 KB aggregate window for batched responses. We can tune based on your UX test.

Pilot asks from Redwood
1) Can you share 1–2 representative sample payloads (sanitized)? I attached a sample_payloads.jsonl file — please replace or confirm.
2) A small list of p95 UX-critical traces (URLs/screens where first-frame matters) so we can prioritize routing.
3) Decision on SSE vs WS for the first pilot (we'll default to SSE if no preference).

Next steps
- If you confirm sampling + SSE pilot, we'll provision a dedicated 2-GPU pool for 72 hours with traffic steering and a synthetic load runner to reproduce your peak.
- Internal kickoff: I’ll loop in Ben (runtime) and Kim (solutions) for detailed sizing and test plan by Monday.

Attachments: clearpay_latency_matrix.xlsx (small matrix of candidate SLO buckets), sample_payloads.jsonl

Jordan — great notes, thanks. A few clarifying items from our side before we lock the pilot scope: 

1) Payload mix: core checks are small (~2 KB). The long notes are rare but important for escalations — we need to ensure 95th for those is reasonable.
2) Throughput: 1.2k/s is peak for internal batch processes, but we only need low single-digit ms latency for those (they're batch). The real UX risk is the interactive reviewer flow (target users) where first-frame matters.
3) SSE vs WS: browser teams prefer SSE for fallback simplicity; mobile teams will likely use WS.

A couple of asks: can Redwood provide an initial costing estimate for the 72-hour dedicated pool (ballpark)? Also, we'd like to see an example of a chunk cadence you recommend for the reviewer flow — how you configure emit windows vs chunk sizes.

I'll sanitize and return the sample payloads by EOD Monday.

Thanks — Alicia

Quick sketch from runtime:

Topology suggestion
- Dedicated pool: 2x A10G nodes (8 GPUs total logical via multi-instance or 4x A100-80GB depending on model variant). Start with 2x A10G for cost/time to iterate, escalate to A100 if p95 misses.
- Autoscale headroom: allow 1.5x burst (so provision 1,500 capacity for 1,000 concurrent target).

SLO tuning rationale
- First-frame: median < 120 ms p95 < 360 ms for <=3 KB — achievable with continuous batching disabled for interactive streams and small fixed prefetch for KV cache.
- For large payloads (>5 KB) we expect median ~180–250 ms p95 ~500–700 ms; we'll quantify in pilot.

Chunk cadence & streaming defaults (pilot)
- Default: SSE with emit window = 60 ms and max chunk size ~32 KB. This yields smooth UX while keeping overhead low.
- Mobile / WS: allow 40 ms window if you need snappier feel and can tolerate slightly higher connection churn.
- Heartbeat: 15s interval, reconnect backoff: immediate, 2s, 5s, 10s, then 30s.

Pilot measurement plan
1) Run synthetic load that mirrors your provided sample_payloads.jsonl for 12 hours to capture p50/p95/p99.
2) In parallel, run a small set of real user sessions (shadow traffic) for 6 hours.
3) Produce a report with per-payload-size latency buckets, token throughput, and CPU/GPU utilization.

Cost ballpark (72h dedicated pool)
- 2x A10G reserved 72h + bandwidth + observability = approximate $12k–$18k (ballpark; final depends on model selection).

I'll prepare a short runbook and test harness by Monday — Kim, can you take the runbook formatting and client hooks?
